organisms.name: Giraffes
organisms.description: Giraffes are tall African mammals. They browse on trees and shrubs, eating leaves and shoots.
organisms.environment_role: As plant-eating browsers, giraffes consume woody plants rather than mainly grazing on grass.
organisms.notes: This card covers the genus. An IUCN specialist assessment recognized four giraffe species in 2025.

organisms.name: Common sunflower
organisms.description: A sunflower head contains many tiny flowers. The central flowers develop into the familiar sunflower seeds.
organisms.habitat: An annual plant native to the southwestern United States and Mexico; also widely cultivated.
organisms.environment_role: Its seeds are used for food and oil, and processing leftovers can be used as feed.
organisms.physical_dimensions: Often around 2 metres tall; cultivated varieties differ.

organisms.name: Baker's yeast
organisms.description: This yeast is a single-celled fungus. During fermentation it can turn sugars into alcohol and carbon dioxide.
organisms.habitat: Found in human-managed fermentations and natural settings including soil and plant surfaces.
organisms.environment_role: Its fermentation activity is used in bread-making and other food and beverage production.
organisms.notes: Its natural ecology is still studied; do not describe fruit as its one established natural niche.

organisms.name: E. coli
organisms.description: E. coli are bacteria. Many kinds live harmlessly in intestines, while some kinds can cause illness.
organisms.habitat: Found in intestines and also in settings such as water, food and the wider environment.
organisms.environment_role: Harmless intestinal kinds can contribute to digestion and vitamin production.
